# One row per LINE, never per file: a row matches only when the file (relative to
# $PORT) is equal AND the line contains the fixed text below. A new pre-move
# literal added to the same file is therefore still CODE. A row whose text no
# longer appears in its file is reported as STALE by --verify, so an exemption
# cannot outlive the line it was written for. Text `*` exempts a whole file, for
# DOC rows only — it never exempts CODE.
# Decided by the operator 2026-09-23 ("do it", on the recommendation table).
# when the scanner graduated into bin/ (harbor#629), verbatim but for two things
# lint forbids in a tracked file, neither of which changes what a row matches:
#   @HOME@ stands for the home directory, and the scanner renders it (lint HP1
#          refuses a tracked file naming its author's home, harbor#602). Write
#          it for any new row that quotes an absolute home path.
# This table holds the rows for harbor's own files (harbor/...), which are also what an installed copy under the config
# dir is judged by. A row for any other repo (a sibling's file, a client's directory) is the private layer's own, in
# `port-paths-exempt.tsv` there, same columns, read after this one (CONTRACTS/private-layer.md). Without it those
# COLUMNS  file <TAB> fixed text on the line <TAB> why it stays
